title: Cost Optimization Strategies
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of cost optimization strategies and its relationship to Performance Optimization and Cloud Cost Management.
Interpret the example and identify at least one prerequisite or boundary relevant to cost optimization strategies.
Propose a safe verification or troubleshooting step and record one security, reliability or cost consideration.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn cost optimization strategies in the context of Performance Optimization and Cloud Cost Management. You will connect the listed subtopics to a practical decision, inspect a small example, and define evidence that would confirm or disprove your assumptions.
content.why_it_matters: Cost Optimization Strategies matters because it is one part of performance and cost management. Real workloads depend on explicit prerequisites, correct permissions, predictable behavior and a way to verify outcomes. Learning the decision points helps you distinguish a working demonstration from a safe and supportable design.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** Cost Optimization Strategies belongs to Performance Optimization and Cloud Cost Management. Measure performance and cost against a workload goal. Use actual usage and cost data, right-size gradually, and remember that a budget alert is not a spending cap.

The PDF lists these subtopics: Removing idle resources; Storage lifecycle management; Capacity planning; Comparing managed versus self-managed services. Treat them as a connected workflow rather than a list to memorize. Start with the workload requirement, identify the AWS resource/control involved, and write down who owns configuration and operation.

content_blocks.title: Practical reasoning
content_blocks.text: **Apply it safely.** For cost optimization strategies, name the prerequisites and the expected result before making a change. Prefer a read-only inspection or local/static example first. Then plan a normal case, a failure case, and a verification step. In a live account, require the account owner-approved sandbox, narrow permissions, spend visibility and cleanup plan. Do not put credentials in code or commit local configuration files.

items.title: Removing idle resources
items.text: Identify the AWS resource or design decision involved, the permissions and prerequisites it needs, and the evidence that shows it is configured as intended.

items.title: Storage lifecycle management
items.text: Document the data shape, access pattern, retention, permissions, recovery path and performance needs. Verify query or storage behavior with representative synthetic data.

items.title: Capacity planning
items.text: Write a verification step and a failure case. For hands-on work, start with read-only inspection and use an approved sandbox before changing cloud resources.

items.title: Comparing managed versus self-managed services
items.text: Record ownership, dependencies and teardown/recovery behavior so the design can be operated safely after the first successful test.

content_blocks.title: Cost decision record: Cost Optimization Strategies
content_blocks.expected_output: A cost/performance record that leaves unknown measurements explicit instead of inventing values.

content_blocks.limitations: The CodeLeaf playground is an HTML/CSS/JavaScript preview and does not execute AWS APIs, shell commands, SQL or cloud deployments. Treat output as illustrative; live values depend on credentials, permissions, Region, service state and schema.

content_blocks.title: Security and cost checkpoint
content_blocks.text: For cost work, a budget notification is not a hard spending cap. Check actual usage and remove approved lab resources.

task: Create a one-page decision card for “Cost Optimization Strategies”. State the goal, prerequisites, the AWS resource or control involved, the expected result, one read-only/static verification step, one failure case, the relevant permission boundary, and cost/cleanup considerations. Do not create or alter billable resources unless the account owner has approved the lab.
hints: Start from the exact subtopics in the lesson and define the desired state in your own words.
Prefer a read-only check or static artifact before a mutating command; record the identity/Region and required permissions.
Verify the expected result and a failure path using current official documentation; write down cost and cleanup implications.
expected_output: A short reviewable decision card for Cost Optimization Strategies with prerequisites, evidence, a failure case, security implications and cost/cleanup notes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one successful example as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: The example may not test permissions, regional/service prerequisites, retries, recovery, quotas or edge cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Write acceptance criteria, test a failure path, inspect logs/state and record the limits of the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing a live resource before confirming its effect and cost.
common_mistakes.why: Cloud changes can expose data, break traffic or leave billable dependencies behind.
common_mistakes.fix: Start read-only, use an approved sandbox, review the change, tag ownership and verify cleanup.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying broad permissions or credentials into source files.
common_mistakes.why: Broad permissions and leaked long-lived credentials increase the impact of mistakes.
common_mistakes.fix: Use scoped roles/temporary credentials, keep secrets in approved stores and review access boundaries.

summary: Cost Optimization Strategies is taught as part of Performance Optimization and Cloud Cost Management.
Measure performance and cost against a workload goal. Use actual usage and cost data, right-size gradually, and remember that a budget alert is not a spending cap.
Verify assumptions with official service documentation and evidence from the relevant AWS resource, logs or tests.
For live labs, confirm permissions and likely charges before acting, then verify cleanup.
